To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of optimized reconstruction parameters for multicentric PET studies is feasible, improves the accuracy of quantitative results, reduces variability between scanners and sites, and is easy to implement.
the optimization of reconstruction parameters for a multicentre study is feasible and leads to a significant improvement in quantitative values.
the optimization of PET acquisition parameters for the MEMENTO study led to an improvement in the quality of PET imaging in the context of a multicentre trial.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of PET neuroimaging for a multicentre study.
the optimization of the reconstruction of PET images.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 22 PET sites involved in the MementO study were able to optimize their acquisition parameters in a way that resulted in improved quantitative values for the 18F-FDG PET images.
the optimized parameters are not better than routine ones, but that they are more reproducible, and that the optimized parameters should therefore be used for multicentre trials.
3D-Osem reconstruction is the most robust and best suited to multicentric PET neuro-imaging trials, with the additional advantage that the reconstruction time is reduced by a factor of 3.5.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimized 3D-OEM reconstruction parameters are a good alternative to routine parameters for the multicentric MEMENTO trial.
the optimization of 3D-OSEMs parameters for multicentric PET studies should be performed using a phantom with hot spheres of different sizes.
the optimized 3D-OSEMs reconstructions are more accurate than the routine ones, but that the gain is limited to the smallest spheres.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimization of 3D-OEM reconstruction parameters is a valuable approach to improving PET quantitative values and reducing variability between centres.
the optimization of the reconstruction parameters can be performed with phantom measurements, without the need for a reference standard.
, in a multicentre setting, the use of optimized parameters for 3D-OEM reconstructions can be recommended to improve the quality of PET quantitative results.
